about: The owner's acceptance part: a SubD pipe clamp, built by the agent's cage tools (apps/cad-studio/test/subdClamp.test.ts) — a thick-walled tube open at both ends with holding loops at its rims, a lug extruded from its wall with a step at one end, a round hole bridged through the lug (its axis square to the tube's) with holding loops at both mouths, the lug's top an arc round the hole. One closed body of genus 2: exact B-spline faces and G1 caps at the extraordinary vertices round the lug and the hole.
oracle: Volume, area and centroid from the independent Catmull–Clark in packages/barocss-cad/test/subd.test.mjs (any polygon, OpenSubdiv's sharp rules; each vertex taken to its limit position), refined 4 and 5 times and extrapolated by Richardson (x5 + (x5 − x4)/3): 16476.1770 mm³, 11019.5217 mm², [4.41189, 0, 19.99865] mm; refined 3 and 4 times the extrapolation differs by 6e-8 and 4e-8. This kernel: 16476.1762 mm³ (5e-8 off), 11019.5254 mm² (3.4e-7), centroid within 3e-6 mm. The tolerances (1e-4, 1e-3 mm) allow another implementation's caps their own small distance from the limit. The subd bounds are the standing SubD promises (D78/D79); this kernel measures: G1 1.9e-6°, gaps 2.2e-14 mm, caps' largest distance from the limit 0.0120 mm (rms 0.0006; 0.0145% of the 83 mm size), smallest |Su × Sv| 0.068 of its cap's median, normals turning 3.3° between grid neighbours; 20 irregular vertices, 88 caps, one Catmull–Clark step.
notes: Known open item, not loosened: the tessellation (8 segments a quarter) has concave folds up to 88.6° (69.7° at 12) between sliver triangles about 0.01 mm high, inside exact B-spline patches along the rims' tight holding loops: the general B-spline face tessellator's D79 to-do (A5), not a fold of the surface or at a cap's boundary (the caps' normals turn at most 3.3°).
